intro.title: useClickOutside
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom Vue composable called `useClickOutside` that detects when a user clicks outside a specific element on the page. You will learn how to use Vue's `ref` and `onMounted`/`onUnmounted` lifecycle hooks to manage DOM event listeners. The core programming concept involves handling click events and checking if the click target is outside a referenced element. By the end, you'll have a reusable composable that can enhance UI components like dropdowns or modals by closing them when a user clicks elsewhere.
intro.usecase: The useClickOutside pattern is essential for creating intuitive UI components that close or hide when users interact elsewhere on the page. You'll see this in production applications when closing dropdown menus after selecting an option, dismissing modal dialogs by clicking outside them, or collapsing search filters in e-commerce interfaces. As a Vue developer, implementing this pattern ensures your interactive elements behave predictably, improving user experience in admin dashboards, form wizards, and navigation systems. Mastering useClickOutside helps you build professional-grade components that respond naturally to user intent.
